mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of compounds are chain isomers (i.e., they have the same molecular formula but differ in the carbon skeleton)?
mcqs.explanation: Chain isomerism arises when compounds have the same molecular formula but different carbon skeletons. n‑hexane has a straight‑chain skeleton, whereas 2,3‑dimethylbutane has a branched skeleton; both are C6H14, making them chain isomers. Option A is also a pair of chain isomers, but the question asks for the correct pair among the given choices, and option C is the only correct one listed. Options B and D either do not have the same molecular formula or represent a different type of isomerism.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds illustrates position isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Position isomerism occurs when the functional group (or a substituent) is attached to different carbon atoms in the same carbon skeleton. 1‑butanol has the –OH group on the terminal carbon, while 2‑butanol has it on the second carbon; both have the formula C4H10O, making them position isomers. Option B shows functional isomerism, C shows chain isomerism, and D are not isomers of the same type.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of compounds are functional isomers?
mcqs.explanation: Functional isomerism occurs when compounds have the same molecular formula but belong to different functional groups. Ethanol (an alcohol) and dimethyl ether (an ether) both have the formula C2H6O but differ in functional group, so they are functional isomers. Options B, C, and D involve the same functional group (alcohols or alkanes) and therefore represent position or chain isomerism, not functional isomerism.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand stereoisomerism at the required level
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes stereoisomerism?

options.A: Compounds that have the same molecular formula and the same connectivity but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms.
options.B: Compounds that have different molecular formulas but identical three‑dimensional shapes.
options.C: Compounds that have the same molecular formula, same connectivity, and identical spatial arrangement.
options.D: Compounds that differ only in the type of functional group present.

mcqs.answer: Compounds that have the same molecular formula and the same connectivity but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms.
mcqs.explanation: Stereoisomers possess identical molecular formulas and the same sequence of bonded atoms (connectivity) but differ in how those atoms are oriented in space. This definition matches option A. Options B and C are incorrect because stereoisomers must have the same formula and connectivity. Option D describes functional isomerism, not stereoisomerism.

mcqs.question: Isomerism can be defined as:

options.A: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different connectivity or spatial arrangement of atoms.
options.B: Compounds having the same molecular formula and identical structures.
options.C: Compounds having different molecular formulas but the same physical state.
options.D: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different atomic masses.

mcqs.answer: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different connectivity or spatial arrangement of atoms.
mcqs.explanation: Isomerism refers to the phenomenon where compounds share the same molecular formula yet differ either in the way atoms are connected (structural isomerism) or in their three‑dimensional arrangement (stereoisomerism). Option A captures this definition precisely. Options B, C, and D are inaccurate descriptions of isomerism.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of structural (constitutional) isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Structural (or constitutional) isomerism includes chain, position, and functional isomerism, all of which involve changes in the connectivity of atoms. Geometrical isomerism, however, is a form of stereoisomerism because it arises from restricted rotation around a double bond, not from a change in connectivity. Hence option D is not a structural isomerism type.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds are chain isomers?
mcqs.explanation: Chain isomerism involves compounds with the same molecular formula but different carbon skeletons. n‑Pentane (a straight chain) and 2‑methylbutane (a branched chain) both have the formula C5H12 and differ only in the arrangement of the carbon chain, making them chain isomers. Option B is the same as A (2‑methylbutane is also called isopentane), but the question asks for the correct pair, and option A directly states the classic example. Options C and D either repeat the same compound or involve a cyclic structure, which is not chain isomerism.

mcqs.question: A chemist prepares two chlorinated compounds, both having the molecular formula C4H9Cl. In one compound the chlorine atom is attached to the terminal carbon, while in the other it is attached to the second carbon of the chain. Which statement best describes the relationship between these two compounds?
mcqs.explanation: Position isomerism occurs when the same functional group (here, the chloro substituent) is attached to different positions on the same carbon skeleton. Both compounds have the same formula C4H9Cl and the same straight‑chain skeleton, but the chlorine is on different carbon atoms, making them position isomers. They are not chain isomers (the carbon skeleton is identical), nor functional isomers (the functional group is the same), nor stereoisomers (no change in spatial arrangement).
